- Marketplace listing: GCP Marketplace (entity billed: Redwood EU Ltd.)

Thanks,

Jonas / team — I pulled the payout ledger for Redwood EU Ltd. and cross-referenced marketplace settlement lines for Q2. Quick summary:

- I don’t see an obvious match for BLSQ2-2026-CREDIT-41 in the April–June settlement CSV we received from GCP.
- There is a negative line (line id ends in -392) on 2026-06-15 for EUR 12,450 but it’s tagged to a different merchant_id (legacy entity) — appears to be an entity mapping issue between our EU and legacy listings.

Next steps I recommend:
- Ask BlueOak for the GCP line-item ID (helps GCP match).
- If BlueOak can provide a signed credit memo we will: 1) create a vendor credit file in the ledger, 2) request GCP to re-associate the negative line to Redwood EU Ltd. or 3) if GCP cannot change history, we can apply an internal offset against the next payout and record a cross-entity adjustment in our ledger.

I uploaded the payout extract and my working reconciliation to Drive: https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1R3cReconcileBlueOak (read-only link to working sheet). I also exported the ledger slice: payout-ledger-export-20260901.csv (attached).

If we go internal-offset route we’ll need:
- BlueOak signed credit memo (PDF)
- Confirmation of marketplace invoice id / merchant id mapping
- Finance approval for cross-entity offset (I’ll queue that, estimate 2 business days once docs are in).

Marissa

Thanks Marissa — that sounds right. A couple operational notes from billing ops:

- GCP marketplace historically will not mutable-apply credits across merchant_ids after settlement — they can reassign line-items in exceptional cases but it takes escalations and a signed vendor credit memo.
- For speed, we prefer to apply the credit internally against the next Redwood EU Ltd. payout and record a contra-revenue adjustment so partner receives the value quickly.
- We need BlueOak to confirm if they accept an internal offset vs. waiting for GCP to reassign (which can take 3–6 weeks).

If BlueOak opts for internal offset, prepare a signed credit memo and the PO/contract reference; we’ll mark it as "Vendor offset — GCP reconciliation" in the ledger and map the contra entry to the BlueOak vendor code. I’ve created a HubSpot ticket to track the approval: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/ticket/HS-98765

Karthik
Billing & Marketplace Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Action plan: applying BlueOak credit to next Redwood EU payout

Ravi — thanks for the quick turnaround earlier. Per our internal review (thread below), Redwood can move forward with an internal offset against the next scheduled payout for Redwood EU Ltd. to expedite credit delivery to BlueOak. To complete the offset we need the following from you:

1) Signed credit memo referencing BLSQ2-2026-CREDIT-41 (PDF).
2) Marketplace invoice or line-item id if available (optional but helpful).
3) PO or contract reference for cross-check (if you have one).

If you can confirm you accept an internal offset (rather than waiting for GCP to reassign history), we’ll:
- Create the vendor credit in our ledger and apply the EUR 12,450 contra entry to the Sep/Oct payout cycle.
- Mark the payment notes with the HubSpot ticket HS-98765 for audit.
- Provide a short confirmation email once the offset is recorded (target: within 48 hours of receiving signed memo).

Please send the signed memo to billing@redwood.com and I’ll escalate for sign-off. Thanks and cc’ing Marissa/Karthik who will track the ledger update.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
